urgency_definitions.urgent: Any of: a safety risk to a person; a situation getting materially worse by the hour; or a firm external deadline falling within about 48 hours where missing it causes irreversible harm such as a failed settlement. Needs attention today.
urgency_definitions.priority: A real deadline within days, or significant financial or legal consequence if it slips. Needs attention this week.
urgency_definitions.routine: Everything else. Handle in normal course.

emails.subject: Dishwasher leaking
emails.body: My dishwasher has been leaking under the kitchen cabinet and the floor is starting to swell. Can you send a plumber please.
emails.note: Appliance inside the lot. Rule 2.4 puts this on the owner. Confusion pair with EM008.

emails.subject: Dog in 12 - again
emails.body: The dog in lot 12 is off lead in the lobby every single morning and there was mess by the lift on Tuesday that nobody cleaned up. I have raised this twice. What are you actually going to do about it?
emails.note: Rule 5.2. Relabelled to requires authority True: the owner is asking what will be done, and enforcement beyond a courtesy reminder needs instruction from the committee. Previously marked contested.

emails.subject: Floorboards
emails.body: Hi, we're renovating and want to put floorboards through the living areas. Do we need to ask anyone or can we just go ahead?
emails.note: Rule 7.2. Works are inside the lot, hence the secondary, but the actual ask is permission. Retrieval currently FAILS on 'floorboards' because the rule says 'hard floor coverings'.

emails.subject: Air conditioner install
emails.body: I want to put an air conditioner in. The condenser would go on the external wall near the courtyard. Is that alright?
emails.note: Rule 2.3, attaching to common property. Retrieval currently ranks rule 2.4 above 2.3 for this wording.

emails.subject: Insurance certificate for my lender
emails.body: My bank is refinancing and has asked for a certificate of currency for the building insurance. Can you email it through?
emails.note: Routine document request.

emails.subject: Following up - certificate for Lot 103
emails.body: Following up on my request from last Tuesday. We still haven't received the owners corporation certificate and the contract is due with the purchaser's solicitor Thursday. Please advise urgently.
emails.note: Escalated follow up with a named Thursday deadline blocking a settlement. Stays urgent, now supported by the deadline clause added to the urgent definition rather than by instinct.

emails.subject: No hot water
emails.body: We've had no hot water since yesterday morning. The unit is the one in the laundry cupboard inside our apartment. Who do I call?
emails.note: Hot water unit inside the lot is the owner's, so the category is private lot. Relabelled routine to priority: a week without hot water is a significant consequence, and responsibility affects category, not urgency.

emails.subject: Lobby door not closing
emails.body: The main lobby door isn't latching properly, it just swings back open. Anyone can walk in off the street.
emails.note: Security implication raises it above routine.

emails.subject: Pothole in the driveway
emails.body: There's a decent pothole forming near the entry. Caught it with my car last week. Not urgent but it's getting bigger.
emails.note: Owner explicitly says not urgent. Tests whether the model listens.

emails.subject: Fence between units
emails.body: The dividing fence between our courtyard and next door is falling over. Who pays for that?
emails.note: Another genuine boundary ambiguity. Should not be answered with false confidence.

emails.subject: Cat
emails.body: We're adopting a cat next month. What do we need to do?
emails.note: Rule 5.1 notification. Deliberate near duplicate of EM023 to test consistency between similar cases.

emails.subject: Certificate - Lot 4 Craigieburn Rise
emails.body: Please provide an owners corporation certificate for Lot 4. No particular rush, the vendor is still deciding on a listing date.
emails.note: Certificate request with NO deadline. Tests whether the model treats the category as automatically urgent.

emails.subject: URGENT certificate
emails.body: URGENT - need the OC certificate for Lot 12 ASAP!!! Client is waiting.
emails.note: TRAP. Shouty and says urgent but names no actual deadline. Tests whether the model reads urgency from tone or from facts.

emails.subject: Special levy
emails.body: I've heard there might be a special levy for the driveway. How much and when? I need to plan for it.
emails.note: Asks about something that may not be decided yet. The agent should not confirm a levy that has not been struck.

emails.subject: Interest charges
emails.body: I've been charged interest on my overdue levies. Can you waive it?
emails.note: Lot 47 is genuinely in arrears. Waiving interest is a decision the manager cannot make alone.

emails.subject: Rubbish in the driveway
emails.body: Someone has dumped an old mattress next to the bins again. Third time this year.
emails.note: Rule 6.2. No named culprit, same shape as the fire door case.

emails.subject: Fob given to strangers
emails.body: The tenant in 88 has been handing out building fobs to their friends. There were four people I didn't recognise in the lift last night.
emails.note: Rule 1.3. Security implication.

emails.subject: Do we even need an AGM
emails.body: There are only six of us and we all get along. Do we actually have to hold a formal AGM every year?
emails.note: TIER DEPENDENT. SCH005 is tier 4. Requires get_scheme.

emails.subject: Insurance for services OC
emails.body: What does the owners corporation insurance cover here? I can't work out what I need my own policy for.
emails.note: TRAP. SCH006 is services only with sum insured 0. Requires get_scheme and an honest answer.

emails.subject: Claim for stolen bike
emails.body: My bike was stolen from the basement storage cage. Does the building insurance cover that?
emails.note: Contents versus building. Also a security question.
